questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: English expressions that compare people to animals
Why gorillas are cleverer than chimpanzees
How scientists teach chimps to use tools
How chimpanzee politics is similar to human politics
questions.why: Sam says chimps have their own politics which is surprisingly similar to human politics.

questions.q: Why does Sam find it strange that nobody says 'as clever as a chimpanzee'?
options: Because chimps are our close cousins and very like us
Because chimps are the cleverest animals of all
Because the expression exists in other languages
Because bees are not very clever
questions.why: He says it's strange because chimpanzees are our close cousins who are most like us.

questions.q: What surprising fact does Neil mention about chimps?
options: They live alone most of the time
They have no leaders
They are more like humans than like gorillas
They are less intelligent than horses
questions.why: Neil asks, 'Did you know that a chimp is more like a human than like a gorilla?'

questions.q: According to Professor Frans de Waal, what do older males who can't be leaders any more do?
options: They leave the group and live alone in the forest
They help a young male become leader
They fight the alpha male together
They look after the babies
questions.why: He says they start grooming a young male with a future and may make him the alpha male.

questions.q: Why do these older males help the young male?
options: Because he is their son
Because they are afraid of him
Because they want more food for the group
So they can keep their own power and influence
questions.why: Neil says older chimps control younger males to maintain their own power and influence.

questions.q: According to Professor Simon Hicks, what should two small parties in a parliament often do?
options: Join the biggest party to share its power
Unite if together they have a majority
Stay in opposition
Hold a new election
questions.why: He says the two smaller ones should get together if together they can reach more than 50% of the seats.

questions.q: Why does Professor Hicks think small parties should avoid joining a big party?
options: The big party would dominate and they'd get few benefits
The big party would refuse to share its voters with them
It is against the law in most countries with elections
Voters always prefer big parties to small ones in the end
questions.why: He says the big party would dominate and they wouldn't get many of the spoils.

questions.q: What behaviour do alpha chimps and human politicians both have, according to Neil?
options: Giving long speeches to large crowds
Hiding food from others in their group
Kissing babies to show their softer side
Avoiding older and stronger males
questions.why: Neil says both like to show their softer side by kissing babies.
